# API reference

<!-- Generated by `make generate` from the doc comments. Do not edit; edit the
     comment and regenerate. `make check-api` and api_test.go fail on a
     diff. -->

A signature index of every public package: the package synopsis, then each
exported identifier with its signature and the first sentence of its doc
comment. A type's constants, variables, constructors and methods are listed
under it. [pkg.go.dev](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/ushineko/sanshoku) has the
full prose.

## sanshoku

`import "github.com/ushineko/sanshoku"`

Package sanshoku is the vocabulary every driver in this module shares: an Identity, a Candidate found by a Driver, an open Device, the sentinel errors, and Scan, which runs a set of drivers and lists what they found.

### Variables

- `var ErrAbsent = errors.New("absent")`: ErrAbsent is nothing to find.
- `var ErrUnavailable = errors.New("unavailable")`: ErrUnavailable is a driver that could not look: the transport it needs is not there (no BlueZ on the bus).
- `var ErrGone = errors.New("device gone")`: ErrGone is a device that was there and is not now.
- `var ErrUnsupported = errors.New("unsupported device")`: ErrUnsupported is a device the driver recognises and will not speak to.

### Types

#### type Bus

```go
type Bus int
```

Bus is the kind of connection a device is found on.

- `const BusUSB Bus = iota + 1`: BusUSB is a device on USB, including one behind a USB receiver.
- `const BusBluetooth Bus`: BusBluetooth is a device on Bluetooth, classic or LE.
- `const BusHwmon Bus`: BusHwmon is a kernel sensor chip under /sys/class/hwmon, which has no bus of its own a program can talk to.
- `func (b Bus) String() string`: String names a bus for the testbench and a consumer's diagnostics.

#### type Candidate

```go
type Candidate struct {
	Identity

	Driver string

	Open func(context.Context) (Device, error)
}
```

Candidate is a device a driver found and has not opened.

- `func Scan(ctx context.Context, drivers ...Driver) ([]Candidate, error)`: Scan runs each driver's Find in order and returns every candidate found.

#### type Describer

```go
type Describer interface {
	Describe() Description
}
```

Describer is a driver that says what it is.

#### type Description

```go
type Description struct {
	Name string

	Finds string

	Capabilities []string

	Platforms []string

	Quiet bool
}
```

Description is what a driver says about itself: what a person knows its devices by, what it looks for, what those devices offer and where it reads them.

- `func Describe(d Driver) (Description, bool)`: Describe is d's description, and false for a driver that gives none -- one written outside this module.
- `func (d Description) Offers(capability string) bool`: Offers reports whether the driver's devices offer capability.
- `func (d Description) On(goos string) bool`: On reports whether the driver reads on goos, as runtime.GOOS spells it.

#### type Device

```go
type Device interface {
	Identity() Identity
	Close() error
}
```

Device is an open handle on one device.

#### type Driver

```go
type Driver interface {
	Name() string
	Find(context.Context) ([]Candidate, error)
}
```

Driver knows one vendor's protocol on one transport and finds the devices that speak it.

#### type Identity

```go
type Identity struct {
	Vendor  uint16
	Product uint16
	Bus     Bus
	Name    string
	Phys    string
	Path    string
}
```

Identity is what a program shows the user about a device and what the testbench keys its report on.

- `func (i Identity) String() string`: String is `Name (vvvv:pppp)`, the form a person reads.

#### type Presence

```go
type Presence struct {
	Nodes int

	Quiet int

	TooOld []string

	OldProtocol string
}
```

Presence is what a receiver holds beyond what could be read: how many of its nodes were opened, how many paired slots were asked and stayed silent, and which devices answered in a protocol too old to read.

- `func (p Presence) Add(q Presence) Presence`: Add is p and q summed: the Presence of two receivers on one desk.

#### type Presencer

```go
type Presencer interface {
	Presence() Presence
}
```

Presencer is a device that reports its Presence.

### Functions

- `func Capabilities(d Device) []string`: Capabilities names the capability interfaces a device satisfies, in a fixed order: "battery", "cooling", "screen", "lighting".
- `func IsPermission(err error) bool`: IsPermission reports a refusal to open anywhere in err's chain: EACCES or EPERM on Linux, ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED on Windows (which matches fs.ErrPermission and neither errno, #39).

## all

`import "github.com/ushineko/sanshoku/all"`

Package all lists every driver in the module, for a program that wants all of them.

### Functions

- `func Drivers() []sanshoku.Driver`: Drivers is every driver in the module, in the order the specs landed them.
- `func Support() []support.Entry`: Support is every driver's support entries, in driver order.

## apple

`import "github.com/ushineko/sanshoku/apple"`

Package apple is the driver for Apple audio accessories (AirPods) over the Accessory Protocol on an L2CAP socket, with per-ear and case levels.

### Variables

- `var ErrNoBatteryPacket = errors.New("the device did not report a battery")`: ErrNoBatteryPacket is a device that connected and never reported, or reported no cell.

### Types

#### type Driver

```go
type Driver struct {
	Timeout time.Duration
}
```

Driver reads Apple audio accessories (AirPods) over the accessory protocol on an L2CAP channel, with per-ear and case levels, and falls back to the device's BlueZ Battery1 level when the channel will not open or the device does not report.

- `func (Driver) Describe() sanshoku.Description`: Describe is what the driver reads: Apple accessories among the Bluetooth devices, over L2CAP, on Linux only.
- `func (d Driver) Find(ctx context.Context) ([]sanshoku.Candidate, error)`: Find returns one candidate per connected BlueZ device that is Apple (Modalias vendor 004C) and audio (an audio- icon or an audio sink profile).
- `func (Driver) Name() string`: Name is "apple".

### Functions

- `func DecodeBattery(packet []byte) ([]battery.Cell, error)`: DecodeBattery reads an accessory-protocol battery packet into its cells, in the order the device sent them.
- `func Support() []support.Entry`: Support is the apple driver's support table.

## aula

`import "github.com/ushineko/sanshoku/aula"`

Package aula is the driver for the battery of an AULA keyboard on its 2.4 GHz receiver: the F75, whose receiver answers a battery question for the keyboard on a vendor report.

### Types

#### type Driver

```go
type Driver struct {
	Timeout time.Duration
}
```

Driver reads an AULA keyboard's battery through its 2.4 GHz receiver.

- `func (Driver) Describe() sanshoku.Description`: Describe is what the driver reads: the AULA F75 through its 2.4 GHz receiver, on Linux and Windows.
- `func (d Driver) Find(context.Context) ([]sanshoku.Candidate, error)`: Find returns one candidate per AULA receiver interface that declares report 0x13 on vendor page 0xFF02.
- `func (Driver) Name() string`: Name is "aula".

### Functions

- `func Decode(r []byte) (battery.Battery, error)`: Decode reads a battery reply into a reading.
- `func Support() []support.Entry`: Support is the aula driver's support table: the one receiver on the allow-list.

## battery

`import "github.com/ushineko/sanshoku/battery"`

Package battery holds the battery reading and the Source capability a device asserts to.

### Types

#### type Band

```go
type Band int
```

Band is a battery as a device without a gauge reports it.

- `const BandUnknown Band = iota`: The bands, low to high.
- `const BandCritical Band`: The bands, low to high.
- `const BandLow Band`: The bands, low to high.
- `const BandGood Band`: The bands, low to high.
- `const BandFull Band`: The bands, low to high.
- `func (b Band) Segments() int`: Segments is how many of four are filled.
- `func (b Band) String() string`: String is the band's word, empty for BandUnknown.

#### type Battery

```go
type Battery struct {
	Name string

	Level    int
	HasLevel bool

	State State

	Band    Band
	HasBand bool

	Kind Kind

	Cells []Cell
}
```

Battery is one device's reading.

#### type Cell

```go
type Cell struct {
	Cell     CellKind
	Level    int
	Charging bool
}
```

Cell is one cell's level.

#### type CellKind

```go
type CellKind int
```

CellKind names one battery inside a device.

- `const Headset CellKind = iota`: Headset is a device that is one piece and has one battery.
- `const Left CellKind`: Left is the left earbud.
- `const Right CellKind`: Right is the right earbud.
- `const Case CellKind`: Case is the charging case, which is often not there at all.
- `func (c CellKind) String() string`: String names a cell for display and for a test's failure message.

#### type Kind

```go
type Kind int
```

Kind is what sort of device a battery belongs to.

- `const KindOther Kind = iota`: KindOther is the zero value and means "not one of the below", which covers a device that did not say as well as one that said something with no case here.
- `const KindMouse Kind`: KindMouse is a mouse, and also a trackball or a touchpad: what they have in common is being the pointing device on the desk.
- `const KindKeyboard Kind`: KindKeyboard is a keyboard, and also a numpad.
- `const KindHeadset Kind`: KindHeadset is a headset or a pair of headphones or earbuds.
- `func (k Kind) String() string`: String names a kind for display and for JSON.

#### type Source

```go
type Source interface {
	Batteries(context.Context) ([]Battery, error)
}
```

Source is a device that can report its batteries.

#### type State

```go
type State int
```

State is what a battery is doing, as distinct from how full it is.

- `const Discharging State = iota`: Discharging is the ordinary case and says nothing worth drawing.
- `const Charging State`: Charging is plugged in and filling.
- `const Full State`: Full is charged, and is separate from Charging because a device says so itself and a panel that showed it as still filling would be wrong for as long as it stayed on the cable.
- `func (s State) String() string`: String names a state for display and for a test's failure message.

### Functions

- `func Product(vendor, name string) string`: Product is a device's name without the vendor's: "SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless" from a SteelSeries driver is "Arctis Nova Pro Wireless".

## bluez

`import "github.com/ushineko/sanshoku/bluez"`

Package bluez lists connected Bluetooth devices through the BlueZ ObjectManager on the system bus, and is the driver for any device exposing org.bluez.Battery1.

### Variables

- `var ErrNoBlueZ = fmt.Errorf("bluez is not answering: %w", sanshoku.ErrUnavailable)`: ErrNoBlueZ is BlueZ not being there to ask: no daemon, no system bus, a machine with no Bluetooth at all.

### Types

#### type Device

```go
type Device struct {
	Path string

	Name string

	Address string

	Vendor  uint16
	Product uint16

	Level    int
	HasLevel bool

	Apple bool
	Audio bool

	Kind battery.Kind
}
```

Device is what BlueZ, or on Windows the Bluetooth stack, knows about one connected device.

- `func Devices(ctx context.Context) ([]Device, error)`: Devices lists every connected device BlueZ knows about, from the system bus's org.bluez ObjectManager.

#### type Driver

```go
type Driver struct{}
```

Driver reads the battery BlueZ already has for a connected device, from org.bluez.Battery1.

- `func (Driver) Describe() sanshoku.Description`: Describe is what the driver reads: connected Bluetooth devices with a battery, through BlueZ on Linux and the Bluetooth stack's device properties on Windows (spec 016).
- `func (Driver) Find(ctx context.Context) ([]sanshoku.Candidate, error)`: Find returns one candidate per connected device that reports a Battery1 level and is not Apple audio.
- `func (Driver) Name() string`: Name is "bluez".

### Functions

- `func Support() []support.Entry`: Support is the bluez driver's support table: one driver-wide entry with no vendor, which support.Lookup matches for any candidate of this driver.

## hidraw

`import "github.com/ushineko/sanshoku/hidraw"`

Package hidraw finds HID interfaces, parses report descriptors, and exchanges reports and feature reports with them.

### Constants

- `const TypeGlobal = 1`: TypeGlobal is the item type of Usage Page and Report ID.
- `const TagUsagePage = 0x0`: TagUsagePage is the global item that sets the usage page.
- `const TagReportID = 0x8`: TagReportID is the global item that declares a report ID.
- `const BusUSB = 0x03`: BusUSB is a device on USB, including one behind a USB receiver.
- `const BusBluetooth = 0x05`: BusBluetooth is a device on Bluetooth.
- `const QueueDepth = 64`: QueueDepth is how many reports the kernel will hold for one open handle.
- `const SplitsReceivers = true`: SplitsReceivers says whether the system gives each device paired to a receiver a node of its own.

### Variables

- `var DevRoot = "/dev"`: DevRoot is where the nodes themselves live, and the usbfs tree under it, for the same reason.
- `var ErrSilent = errors.New("no reply")`: ErrSilent is an exchange that ran out of time with no matching reply.
- `var SysRoot = "/sys/class/hidraw"`: SysRoot is where the kernel lists hidraw nodes.

### Types

#### type Handle

```go
type Handle struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Handle is an open hidraw node.

- `func Open(path string) (*Handle, error)`: Open opens a hidraw node for reading and writing.
- `func (h *Handle) Close() error`: Close closes the node.
- `func (h *Handle) Drain(depth int)`: Drain discards up to depth reports that arrived before the question was asked.
- `func (h *Handle) GetFeature(ctx context.Context, report []byte) error`: GetFeature reads a feature report into report, whose first byte is the report ID to ask for.
- `func (h *Handle) Read(ctx context.Context, buf []byte) (int, error)`: Read reads one input report into buf.
- `func (h *Handle) SetFeature(ctx context.Context, report []byte) error`: SetFeature sends a feature report, report ID first.
- `func (h *Handle) Write(report []byte) error`: Write sends one output report, report ID first where the device numbers its reports.

#### type Item

```go
type Item struct {
	Type  byte
	Tag   byte
	Value uint32
}
```

Item is one short item of a report descriptor: its type (main 0, global 1, local 2), its tag, and its data read little-endian.

#### type Node

```go
type Node struct {
	Path string

	Name string

	Phys string

	Vendor  uint16
	Product uint16

	Bus uint16

	Descriptor []byte

	Reports []Report

	USBPath string
}
```

Node is one HID interface: where it is and what the system says about it.

- `func Nodes(vendor uint16, want func(Node) bool) ([]Node, error)`: Nodes lists the hidraw nodes of one vendor that satisfy want.

#### type Report

```go
type Report struct {
	Kind  ReportKind
	ID    byte
	Page  uint16
	Usage uint16
	Len   int
}
```

Report is one report a node declares: which way it goes, its number, the usage it carries and how long it is.

#### type ReportDevice

```go
type ReportDevice interface {
	Write(report []byte) error
	Read(ctx context.Context, buf []byte) (int, error)
}
```

ReportDevice is what Exchange speaks through: a *Handle, or a test's stand-in for one.

#### type ReportKind

```go
type ReportKind byte
```

ReportKind is which way a report travels.

- `const ReportInput ReportKind = iota + 1`: ReportInput is a report the device sends.
- `const ReportOutput ReportKind`: ReportOutput is a report the host sends with a write.
- `const ReportFeature ReportKind`: ReportFeature is a report exchanged with a feature request.
- `func (k ReportKind) String() string`: String names a kind for a test's message and the testbench.

### Functions

- `func Exchange(ctx context.Context, dev ReportDevice, req []byte, matches func(reply []byte) bool, size int) ([]byte, error)`: Exchange writes req and returns the first report, read into a buffer of size bytes, for which matches is true, skipping every other report until the context's deadline.
- `func HasReportID(page uint16, id byte) func(Node) bool`: HasReportID is a predicate for Nodes: the node declares report id while the current usage page is page or above.
- `func PairedChild(phys string) bool`: PairedChild reports whether a node is one device behind a receiver rather than the receiver itself.
- `func PairedIndex(phys string) (index byte, ok bool)`: PairedIndex returns the device index a paired child's HID_PHYS ends in, the N of `:N`, and whether there is one.
- `func UsagePage(want uint16) func(Node) bool`: UsagePage is a predicate for Nodes: the node declares the given usage page anywhere in it.
- `func Walk(desc []byte, visit func(item Item) bool)`: Walk reads a report descriptor item by item, calling visit for each until it returns false.

## hwmon

`import "github.com/ushineko/sanshoku/hwmon"`

Package hwmon reads temperatures from /sys/class/hwmon by chip name and label, never by the hwmon index the kernel renumbers.

### Variables

- `var CPU = []Sensor{…}`: CPU are the processor temperatures this module knows, most wanted first.
- `var ErrNoSensor error = absent("no such sensor on this machine")`: ErrNoSensor is a sensor this machine does not have.
- `var GPU = []Sensor{…}`: GPU are the kernel's ways of knowing a graphics card's temperature, in the order they are tried.
- `var Root = "/sys/class/hwmon"`: Root is where the kernel puts its sensors.

### Types

#### type Driver

```go
type Driver struct{}
```

Driver lists the hwmon chips present, so a scan shows the whole machine.

- `func (Driver) Describe() sanshoku.Description`: Describe is what the driver reads: the kernel's sensor chips, on Linux, which alone has hwmon (spec 014).
- `func (Driver) Find(context.Context) ([]sanshoku.Candidate, error)`: Find returns one candidate per chip under Root, ErrAbsent when there are none.
- `func (Driver) Name() string`: Name is "hwmon".

#### type Sensor

```go
type Sensor struct {
	Chip string

	Label string
}
```

Sensor is one labelled temperature the kernel already exposes.

- `func First(root string, sensors []Sensor) (Sensor, float64, error)`: First returns the first of sensors that reads under root, and its value in degrees.
- `func (s Sensor) Read(root string) (float64, error)`: Read is the sensor's temperature in degrees under root: the chip found by its name, then the sensor by its label.
- `func (s Sensor) String() string`: String is chip/label, or the chip alone for an unlabelled sensor: the form an error names a sensor in.

### Functions

- `func Support() []support.Entry`: Support is the hwmon sensor tables as support entries.

## l2cap

`import "github.com/ushineko/sanshoku/l2cap"`

Package l2cap dials Bluetooth L2CAP sequenced-packet sockets with a deadline.

### Types

#### type Conn

```go
type Conn struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Conn is an open L2CAP sequenced-packet channel.

- `func Dial(ctx context.Context, addr [6]byte, psm uint16) (*Conn, error)`: Dial opens an L2CAP channel to a device's port psm.
- `func (c *Conn) Close() error`: Close ends the conversation.
- `func (c *Conn) Receive(ctx context.Context) ([]byte, error)`: Receive waits for one packet until the context's deadline, six seconds when it has none.
- `func (c *Conn) Send(p []byte) error`: Send writes one packet.

### Functions

- `func ParseAddress(s string) ([6]byte, error)`: ParseAddress reads a printed Bluetooth address, "A1:B2:C3:D4:E5:F6", into the order Dial wants, which is the order it is written.

## logitech

`import "github.com/ushineko/sanshoku/logitech"`

Package logitech is the driver for Logitech HID++ 1.0 and 2.0 batteries over hidraw.

### Types

#### type Driver

```go
type Driver struct {
	Timeout time.Duration
}
```

Driver reads Logitech batteries over HID++ 1.0 and 2.0 on hidraw.

- `func (Driver) Describe() sanshoku.Description`: Describe is what the driver reads: Logitech receivers and their devices, on Linux and Windows (spec 012).
- `func (d Driver) Find(context.Context) ([]sanshoku.Candidate, error)`: Find returns one candidate per Logitech hidraw node that speaks HID++: a node whose descriptor declares report 0x10 on a vendor usage page.
- `func (Driver) Name() string`: Name is "logitech".

#### type Presence

```go
type Presence = sanshoku.Presence
```

Presence is what is on a HID++ node beyond what could be read: the root package's, since spec 014, so a consumer reads it with no import of this driver.

#### type Presencer

```go
type Presencer = sanshoku.Presencer
```

Presencer is a device that reports its Presence: sanshoku.Presencer, which a logitech Device satisfies.

### Functions

- `func DecodeBatteryStatus(p []byte) (battery.Battery, error)`: DecodeBatteryStatus reads the parameters of a feature 0x1000 (Battery Status) function 0 reply, which is what a device without a fuel gauge has instead of 0x1004.
- `func DecodeUnifiedBattery(p []byte) (battery.Battery, error)`: DecodeUnifiedBattery reads the parameters of a feature 0x1004 (Unified Battery) function 1 reply: the bytes after the report ID, device index, feature index and function.
- `func Support() []support.Entry`: Support is the logitech driver's support table.

## steelseries

`import "github.com/ushineko/sanshoku/steelseries"`

Package steelseries is the driver for SteelSeries battery readings over hidraw, with a product allow-list: rivalcfg's keyboards and mice (spec 003) and the Arctis Nova Pro Wireless headset through its base station (spec 006).

### Types

#### type Driver

```go
type Driver struct {
	Timeout time.Duration
}
```

Driver reads SteelSeries batteries over hidraw.

- `func (Driver) Describe() sanshoku.Description`: Describe is what the driver reads: SteelSeries keyboards, mice and headsets, on Linux and Windows.
- `func (d Driver) Find(context.Context) ([]sanshoku.Candidate, error)`: Find returns one candidate per SteelSeries hidraw node whose descriptor declares usage page 0xFFC0.
- `func (Driver) Name() string`: Name is "steelseries".

### Functions

- `func DecodeModern(reply []byte) (battery.Battery, error)`: DecodeModern reads the two-byte reply to the modern battery command, 0x92 or 0xD2: the echoed command, then the value.
- `func DecodeNovaPro(reply []byte) (battery.Battery, error)`: DecodeNovaPro reads the Arctis Nova Pro Wireless base station's reply to `06 b0`: the headset's level in byte 6 on a scale of 0 to 8, and its status in byte 15.
- `func Support() []support.Entry`: Support is the steelseries driver's support table, one entry per product in the allow-list.

## support

`import "github.com/ushineko/sanshoku/support"`

Package support is the hardware support table: one Entry per device or protocol a driver speaks, with the tier it has reached (tested on named hardware, expected to work by protocol, or listed and not implemented).

### Types

#### type Entry

```go
type Entry struct {
	Driver string

	Device string

	Match string

	Vendor uint16

	Products []uint16

	Chips []string

	Capabilities []string

	Tier Tier

	Hardware string
	Firmware string

	Tested time.Time

	Spec int

	Notes string

	Windows *Port
}
```

Entry is one row of the support table: a device, or a protocol family, that a driver speaks.

- `func Lookup(entries []Entry, driver string, vendor, product uint16, name string) (Entry, bool)`: Lookup finds the entry that covers a found device, for a program or the bench that wants to say what tier it is at.

#### type Port

```go
type Port struct {
	Tier Tier

	Tested time.Time

	Notes string
}
```

Port is where an entry stands on an operating system other than Linux.

#### type Tier

```go
type Tier int
```

Tier is how far a device's support has got.

- `const Tested Tier = iota`: Tested is a device the testbench has run against, on the hardware the entry names, with the output recorded in the entry's spec.
- `const Expected Tier`: Expected is a device whose protocol is generic and whose code path exists, and which no device has confirmed yet.
- `const Listed Tier`: Listed is a device recognised by ID and not implemented; its Open returns sanshoku.ErrUnsupported.
- `func (t Tier) String() string`: String names a tier, lower case.

## usbfs

`import "github.com/ushineko/sanshoku/usbfs"`

Package usbfs claims a USB interface through /dev/bus/usb and writes to a bulk endpoint with raw usbdevfs ioctls.

### Types

#### type Interface

```go
type Interface struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Interface is a claimed interface on a USB device.

- `func Open(path string, iface int) (*Interface, error)`: Open claims an interface on a USB device node.
- `func (u *Interface) Bulk(ctx context.Context, endpoint byte, data []byte) error`: Bulk writes data to an OUT endpoint, in chunks.
- `func (u *Interface) Close() error`: Close releases the interface and closes the device node.
